title: Rear-end collision
image_prompt: Create a realistic but clearly fictional insurance claim illustration: two ordinary passenger cars after a low-speed rear-end collision at a city traffic light, visible front bumper damage on the rear car, daylight, no people, no logos, no license plate text, no readable text, neutral documentary photo style.

policy.text: For this synthetic case, assume the vehicle is shown on the declarations, the loss occurs during the policy period, and collision coverage and premium are in force.
policy.source_section: Fictional case assumption — not an insurer-issued declaration

policy.text: If collision coverage is purchased, direct accidental loss to a covered vehicle caused by collision with another object or overturning is covered, subject to the applicable limit and deductible.
The policy excludes loss resulting from intentional acts of the insured or family member.

claimant_facts.incident: The insured car struck the rear of another car while approaching a traffic light.
claimant_facts.damage: The front bumper and hood are dented; the repair estimate is $2,800.
claimant_facts.other_facts: The insured driver was driving, no one was injured, and the damage was accidental.

expected.rationale: Under the stated fictional declarations assumption, the reported accidental collision meets the collision insuring agreement, subject to the complete policy and investigation.

policy_source.title: Integon Preferred Insurance Company, California Personal Automobile Policy, form CAIP400 (03/01/2006)
policy_source.note: Historical 2006 form; terms below are short paraphrases of selected sections, not a complete policy. Declarations for this demo are fictional.

title: Same client visit, surcharge present

policy.text: Fictional declarations: listed vehicle, active policy at loss, collision and other-than-collision premiums paid. No other relevant endorsements. The declarations expressly include a business-use surcharge for this vehicle.
policy.source_section: Fictional case assumption — not an insurer-issued declaration

policy.text: If collision coverage is purchased, direct accidental loss to a covered vehicle caused by collision with another object or overturning is covered, subject to the applicable limit and deductible.

Business use other than farming or ranching is excluded, apart from the listed exception when the declarations show a business-use surcharge and the vehicle is used by the insured, family member, or their partner, agent, or employee. The separate motor-business exclusion still applies.

claimant_facts.incident: While driving to a client meeting for my consulting business, I accidentally backed into a post.
claimant_facts.other_facts: I am the named insured; no paid transport, delivery, vehicle repair or other motor business was involved.

expected.rationale: The stated surcharge and named-insured use satisfy the business-use exception; accidental collision remains covered.

title: Burst pipe soaked personal belongings
image_prompt: Realistic fictional insurance documentation photograph. No people, readable text, logos, or paperwork. Living room with wet swollen books on a low shelf, dark saturated rug and stained fabric chair; small puddle, no people, no car.

policy.text: Fictional declarations: renters Coverage C is active for the insured personal belongings at this occupied primary residence at the time of loss. Selected form terms below govern this benchmark; no other modifying endorsement is assumed.
policy.source_section: Fictional case assumption — not an insurer-issued declaration

policy.text: Accidental discharge from a plumbing system or household appliance is a listed peril for covered personal property. The leaking system or appliance itself is not covered by this peril; other listed restrictions still apply.
policy.source_section: HO 00 04 05 11 — Section I, Perils Insured Against 12

policy_source.title: Goodcover California renters sample, HO 00 04 05 11 and listed endorsements
policy_source.note: Public software-testing sample explicitly marked not a valid insurance policy. Selected real form provisions are paraphrased for synthetic cases; declarations and endorsement applicability below are fictional assumptions, not insurer-issued coverage.

claimant_facts.incident: A supply pipe suddenly burst while I was home and soaked my own books, rug and fabric chair. I saw water spraying from the broken pipe.
claimant_facts.damage: Books are swollen and wet, the rug is saturated, and the chair upholstery has water stains.
claimant_facts.other_facts: I shut off the water and reported it immediately. No freezing, mold, external flood or gradual seepage was involved. I claim only my belongings, not pipe repair or building damage.

expected.rationale: Direct damage to covered belongings from the stated sudden plumbing discharge meets the selected peril; the leaking pipe itself is not claimed.

challenge: Contents versus excluded pipe repair; photo does not establish cause
